about: Weekly 'What's new in urology' digest. Built every Monday by tools/weekly-news.mjs from PubMed and merged by pull request. Items marked pinned are hand-picked recent advances. Do not overwrite this file from an app upload.

items.title: AUA releases its 2026 guideline on LUTS attributed to BPH
items.summary: 62 statements across evaluation, medical and procedural care. Medical therapy: offer alfuzosin, silodosin or tamsulosin; a 5-ARI for prostates over 30 mL or PSA over 1.5 ng/mL; daily tadalafil 5 mg; storage drugs alone or with an α-blocker.
items.why: Doxazosin and terazosin drop out of the 'offer' list; tadalafil gains a defined first-line role.

items.title: EAU Urological Infections 2026: new fungal UTI chapter and updated biopsy prophylaxis
items.summary: A limited update adds a chapter on diagnosis and treatment of fungal urinary tract infection, revises antibiotic doses, and updates periprocedural prophylaxis for prostate biopsy, favouring the transperineal route with less antibiotic use.
items.why: Changes candiduria and prostate biopsy prophylaxis practice; see Drugs: Urinary Infections.

items.title: Gepotidacin: first new oral antibiotic class for uncomplicated UTI in about 30 years
items.summary: FDA approval (March 2025), followed by the UK MHRA, for uncomplicated UTI in females aged 12 or over weighing at least 40 kg: 1500 mg twice daily for 5 days. EAGLE-2 and EAGLE-3 showed non-inferiority to nitrofurantoin.
items.why: A new option when resistance or intolerance limits standard cystitis antibiotics; GI side effects are common.

items.title: NOSTONE: hydrochlorothiazide did not prevent recurrent calcium stones
items.summary: Placebo-controlled trial of hydrochlorothiazide 12.5, 25 or 50 mg daily in recurrent calcium stone formers: no dose reduced symptomatic or radiological recurrence over about 3 years; hypokalaemia, gout and new diabetes were more common.
items.why: Challenges routine thiazide prescribing for stone prevention; select patients carefully.

items.title: TRAVERSE: testosterone therapy and cardiovascular safety
items.summary: In hypogonadal men with or at high risk of cardiovascular disease, testosterone gel was non-inferior to placebo for major adverse cardiac events, but atrial fibrillation, acute kidney injury and pulmonary embolism were more frequent.
items.why: Reassures on MACE in properly diagnosed men while highlighting specific risks to counsel about.

items.title: ALTAR: methenamine hippurate vs daily antibiotics to prevent recurrent UTI
items.summary: Open-label non-inferiority trial in women with recurrent UTI: methenamine hippurate 1 g twice daily was non-inferior to low-dose daily antibiotic prophylaxis over 12 months.
items.why: Supports a non-antibiotic first choice for prophylaxis, helping antibiotic stewardship.
